title: Latency sentinel runway and team sprint notes
body:
Purpose
This is a compact reference for a targeted rollout that prioritizes latency stability across the fleet. Use for the upcoming 72hr window (Week of 2026-11-08). It contains preflight checks, a light rollout calendar (shift-slate), a telemetry sampling plan, and a draft release notes blurb.

Scope and constraints
- Surface area: hosted inference endpoints (api/v1/generate) and the dedicated pool autoscaler hook.
- Goal: keep p95 inference latency within baseline +/- 15% during rollout.
- Rollout modality: staged percentage ramp across regions (US-East, US-West, eu-west1) with automatic rollback on sentinel breach.
- Expected risk: short CPU/GPU scheduling thundering on shard increments; KV cache warmup latency spikes.

Quick glossary
- Latency sentinel: a telemetry-derived metric composite that includes p95, 90th token generation time, and queue depth.
- Dark traffic: 1% of live traffic mirrored to new variant for early signal without customer impact.
- Safety lane: route to previous stable model variant and lower concurrency profile.

Preflight checklist (must be green before start)
- [ ] CI green for runtime and autoscaler PRs (PR #982) 
- [ ] Canary instance deployed in staging and passed smoke generator (10k tokens over 30 min)
- [ ] KV cache profiling run: baseline cache hit-rate vs expected workload (attach log)
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards created and shared with on-call rotation (link above)
- [ ] Rollback playbooks and runbook owner assigned (Tom B)
- [ ] Safety lane and throttles configured in routing policy (config id: route-2026-11-latency)
- [ ] Pager policy reviewed and tiny blast radius agreed (2x notify threshold)
- [ ] External customer-facing release note drafted and approved by comms (see draft below)

72hr rollout runway (high level shift-slate)
- Day 0 (Kickoff window, prefer low traffic 02:00–05:00 local):
  - 00:00: Begin traffic mirroring (dark traffic 1%) to new variant in US-East.
  - 01:00: Evaluate sentinel; if green, bump to 5% dark in US-East.
  - 03:00: Start smoke test suite across regions (latency, accuracy quick-check).
  - 05:00: Wait for 6 hours of stable telemetry before moving to step 2.
- Day 1 (Staged rollout):
  - 06:00: US-East: gradual ramp from 0% -> 10% live using weighted routing over 2 hours.
  - 09:00: If p95 <= baseline*1.15 and error rate unchanged, increase to 25%.
  - 14:00: If stable for 6 hours, US-West begins mirror->10% live ramp.
  - 20:00: eu-west1 begins mirror->5% live ramp (lower early ramp for EU regulator traffic).
- Day 2 (Scale and observe):
  - 00:00: Autoscaler policy adjusted upward for dedicated pool burst capacity (+10% headroom).
  - 08:00: Full 50% cross-region ramp target if all sentinels passed.
  - 18:00: If all clear, schedule final cutover to 100% at low-traffic slice on Day 3.
- Day 3 (Finish/rollback window):
  - 02:00: Final cutover to 100% or run controlled slow increase and mark as paused if any threshold triggered.
  - 06:00: Begin wind-down of monitoring shift and hand back to normal on-call.

Sentinel thresholds and automatic actions (ops automation)
- Soft alert (notify rotation): p95 > baseline * 1.10 for 10 consecutive minutes OR token-gen-90th > baseline*1.12. Action: page on-call, reduce ramp rate, enable additional telemetry sampling.
- Hard alert (auto rollback): p95 > baseline * 1.25 for 5 minutes OR queue depth > 3x baseline. Action: automated reroute to safety lane, rollback to previous variant, enlarge autoscaler headroom if safe rollback path fails.
- Error spike: >= 0.5% increase in 4xx/5xx over baseline for 5 minutes triggers immediate canary pause and dark traffic rollback.

Telemetry sampling plan (to limit costs but keep signal)
- Default sampling: 0.5% of tokens captured for full trace (stack traces, model logits) across all traffic.
- Ramp-phase: increase to 5% of requests for variant under test and 0.5% for control to measure delta. Sampling applies to first-10 tokens + every nth token = 5 token windows.
- Attachments retained for 72 hours in short-term storage, 30 days for aggregated metrics only.
- Quick-check probes: synthetic generation probes every 5 minutes per region with fixed prompt set. Results posted to #release-latency channel.

Smoke checklist (minimal runnable checks)
- [ ] Fast parse: warmup request with 128 tokens returns under baseline p95 target.
- [ ] Attachment passthrough: tool call simulation returns correct JSON schema.
- [ ] Model fidelity spot-check: 10 pre-approved prompts run, compare BLEU/surrogate heuristics for regressions.
- [ ] KV cache warmup: run 3 warmup sequences and confirm cache hit rate >= 60% after warmup.
- [ ] Autoscaler sanity: simulate scale-up and scale-down event in staging and confirm config applied.

Operational notes and runbook pointers
- On-call sequence: primary (on-call engineer) -> secondary -> release-owner (Lina) -> Director oncall if escalated beyond 30m.
- Slack channels: #release-latency (ops comms), #release-postmortems (post-run notes).
- Dashboard links: latency composite dashboard (add to bookmarks), routing policy viewer, autoscaler view.
- Telemetry quick commands: 
  - /probe-run (runs synthetic probes)
  - /dump-queue (retrieves queue depth snapshot)
  - /snapshot-variant (capture a 5m sample window)

Draft public-facing release notes (short)
- Title: Gradual latency-stabilized rollout for inference endpoint
- Summary: Over the next 72 hours we will incrementally roll out an updated serving variant that improves scheduling efficiency for medium-length prompts. The rollout is staged and monitored; customers should not see degradation. If you experience increased latency, please open a support ticket with your request id and timestamp.

Internal release notes (expanded)
- Why: small scheduler and KV cache adjustments reduce p50 for 256–512 token workloads; objective is cost-neutral or lower while maintaining p95 SLA.
- What changed: scheduler backpressure smoothing + small reordering of chunked kernel dispatch; config: route-2026-11-latency.
- Rollback criteria: automated on sentinel breach; manual revert via routing console if persistent.

Open questions / TODOs (capture quick hits)
- [ ] Confirm retention policy with privacy before increasing sampling to 5% for test variant. (Ravi)
- [ ] Re-run synthetic probe set B with new prompt mix; results by 2026-11-06 (Naomi)
- [ ] Add explicit note in customer-facing message about expected minor warmup delay for first requests after cutover. (Comms)
- [ ] Finalize canary decision tree in playbook (Tom)

Post-rollout retrospective checklist (to complete within 7 days)
- [ ] Compile p50/p95/p99 comparison across regions and variants.
- [ ] Annotate any user-reported tickets and correlate with telemetry windows.
- [ ] Update autoscaler and route config if regression attributable to mis-tuned headroom.
- [ ] Draft a short postmortem if sentinel triggered any rollbacks (include timeline and remediation).

Notes to the team (informal)
- Keep communication tight and short during ramps. Use the thread-summary pattern for each hour of ramp: "hour-X: key metrics + decisions".
- If you see KV-cache warming showing a long tail, prefer pausing the ramp rather than forcing headroom — we want to observe steady-state behavior.

Appendix: quick command snippets
- Pause rollout (routing CLI): rctl rollout pause --id route-2026-11-latency
- Rollback to previous variant: rctl rollout rollback --id route-2026-11-latency --to previous
- Increase probe sampling: telemetry set-sampling --variant test-2026-11 --rate 0.05

End of doc - keep this as the canonical short-run playbook for the latency-sensitive sprint.

Revision history
- 2026-11-02 Lina Moreno: created draft and initial checks
- 2026-11-03 Ravi Shah: added sampling constraints and open privacy TODO
- 2026-11-05 Tom Becker: tightened sentinel thresholds and added automation CLI commands
